about: Completed intermediates and the scalar kinds of untyped intermediate derivations (LOOKUP-5, LOOKUP-7, LOOKUP-9, LOOKUP-15 to LOOKUP-18, FORMULA-5, TIME-14, VALUE-10, COLUMN-14). An intermediate no column reads still runs its checks and derivations; an earlier intermediate's key or filter reads the record of the donor that reads it; a SELF intermediate's derivations read completed rows; a range, or an aggregate's range, reads a qualified value only where that value's input drives the reading row or donor record; a case branch counts the handlers of the reads it selects; and an untyped selector, choice, alias or key keeps its date, number or unknown kind for the reads after it, which check and build judge alike. Moved from execution_completed_intermediates.rs, which keeps its benchmark reads and the reader of completed_lookup_assertions.json, and from intermediate_result_kinds.rs. A case whose test projected each issue to its phase, condition, rule, spec paths and context names those in compares, and a case whose test read some fields of each issue names those. Where a test read only a prefix or the first of an issue's spec paths, the whole list is derived: an overflow in the unread intermediate's derivation NEXT is at that derivation's path alone, as lookup_matched_derivations.json states for SHIFTED, and each correlated unique refusal has the one path that negative-unique-correlated-filter and negative-unique-correlated-derivation state. A check case writes the specification alone, since a check reads no study input, as the kinds tests checked before writing ex.csv. A test that checked and built one specification is a check case and a build or save case, or one case of both operations where both report the same issues, as for the refusal of a first template's read, which its test required before the run. A handler ledger is the report's handler rows at SPEC_PATH, NAME and COUNT (CHECK-23, CHECK-24), the spec_path, handler and count its test compared. The documents are the specifications several cases edit: kinds writes the derivation EXENDT as DERIVATION, which each case replaces, kinds_anchored also compares EXENDT with the date ANCHOR and writes TRTEDT as text, and kinds_shift shifts EXSTDT by the days SELECTED derives, SELECTED written as DERIVATION.
